drills.q: A VP says 'build AI summaries in the dashboard.' Give the two questions you ask before any architecture discussion.
drills.a: 'What user behavior would tell us this worked?' (outcome) and 'What problem does that outcome imply — who hurts today, how often, at what cost?' (problem). You're walking UP the chain from their solution before evaluating it.

drills.q: Rewrite this as an outcome: 'Ship report summaries by end of Q3 with 95% coverage.'
drills.a: Something like: 'Raise report-follow-through (reports leading to an export/share/action within 48h) from 12% to 18% within two quarters, without degrading p95 load time beyond +100ms.' Behavior + baseline + magnitude + timeframe + guardrail.

drills.q: Compute the annual COGS of an AI feature: 5M requests/month, 1,500 tokens/request, $3 per million tokens.
drills.a: 5e6 x 1500 = 7.5B tokens/mo = 7,500 Mtok x $3 = $22.5K/mo = $270K/yr. The feature must plausibly move >$270K/yr of value to clear its own floor.

drills.q: Your recsys gave +25% engaged interactions. List the full translation chain to revenue and label each link's confidence.
drills.a: +25% interactions -> +20% session length (measured, high confidence) -> +5pts D7 return rate (cohort correlation, medium) -> ARPU via LTV model ($0.31/D7 pt/mo, modeled, weakest link) -> 5pts x $0.31 x 4.2M MAU ~= $6.5M/mo face; present a $4-8M/yr band.

drills.q: A proposal's best case is $300K/yr and needs 2 engineers for 2 quarters plus inference spend. What do you do?
drills.a: Build the one-page ledger: fully loaded opportunity cost ~$400-600K exceeds best-case value even before run-cost. Present arithmetic, not opinion, plus a cheap probe whose result would have to be wildly positive to change the math — and let the review conclude 'not yet'.

drills.q: Write the kill condition for an AI study-buddy feature in a tutoring app.
drills.a: Example: 'If after 4 weeks fewer than 15% of new sessions include a study-buddy interaction, or follow-through-to-next-action doesn't rise >=2pts vs matched cohorts, we cut it.' Specific threshold + timeframe + cheaply observable metric, written before build start.

drills.q: Sales promised a customer a bespoke feature that would create a money-losing one-off architecture. Walk your response.
drills.a: First extract the job the customer is hiring the feature for; check for a cheaper path solving the same need. If the custom work is structurally bad, put lifetime numbers side by side in writing and reframe as pricing: take it as paid professional services or negotiate reference rights so the loss is deliberate and capped.

drills.q: Feature shipped on time, adoption fine, target metric flat. Diagnose in order.
drills.a: (1) Adoption without behavior change — check depth-of-use not activation; (2) outcome dominated by other drivers — segment; affected cohort may have moved 20% but be 4% of base; (3) the original theory linking feature to outcome was wrong. Cohort cuts before theory. Then re-price ongoing cost against the smaller-than-hoped benefit.

drills.q: Translate p95 latency -400ms on a checkout flow into dollars, stating your assumptions.
drills.a: Use a fitted elasticity, not folklore: assume ~0.5% conversion per 100ms (conservative vs commonly cited 1%/100ms figures). On $40M/yr checkout GMV: 4 units of 100ms x 0.5% = ~2% relative... applied conservatively as 2% of $40M ~= $800K/yr, banded and labeled modeled-until-fitted-on-our-own-funnel-data.

drills.q: Three candidate projects, one quarter. Describe the selection artifact you build and the tie-breaker.
drills.a: One page each: problem statement, outcome + baseline, three solution candidates, cheapest path to evidence, kill condition, value-per-week arithmetic. Compare expected annualized value band vs weeks-to-first-evidence. On value ties prefer optionality/reversibility — failure leaves reusable infra, success doesn't lock the roadmap.
